findings.evidence: The manifest producer hashes retained classifications in their normative level-rank, kind-rank, rule, path, locator, fingerprint order. Replay instead loads the relational rows with OrderBy(Fingerprint) at lines 101-105 and feeds that sequence unchanged into manifest tag 26 at lines 526-527. ClassificationsMatch separately sorts only the supplied list by fingerprint, so it can accept row equality before StoredManifestFingerprintMatches recomputes a different manifest for any valid multi-classification package whose semantic order differs from digest order. Such an exact acknowledgement-loss retry returns Conflict at lines 111-113 rather than Replay. The PostgreSQL and SQLite retained-classification tests persist exactly one classification and do not retry it, while the independently run focused suites passed 9/9 and therefore leave this multi-row ordering case unobserved. QR-001's typed CodeGraph/Java preimages, stored proof digest comparisons, manifest scalars, entries, audits, classification contents, and duration-only variance are otherwise corrected, but its complete ordered-manifest reconstruction outcome is not fully closed.
findings.correction_outcome: Reconstruct retained classifications in the exact normative order from canonical typed row fields, or persist and constrain an explicit canonical classification ordinal, and use that same order for both row equality and manifest tag 26. Add a PostgreSQL regression with at least two valid classifications deliberately having different normative and fingerprint orders: commit, clear or replace the DbContext to model restart, and prove exact retry is Replay with zero mutation. Retain conflict tests for missing, extra, changed, and noncanonical classification rows and retain all QR-001 typed-proof/scalar tamper and duration-only replay qualifications.

summary: REVISE. Raw QR-001 is substantially but not fully closed. The corrected candidate durably stores every stable CodeGraph and Java proof preimage, reconstructs both proof envelopes, compares stored and supplied proof identities, includes the previously omitted manifest scalars, and preserves duration-only replay variance; the migration, configuration, snapshot, and typed tamper tests are aligned. However, complete manifest reconstruction uses fingerprint order for persisted Communication Kind Classifications instead of the normative classification order used when the manifest was created. A common valid multi-classification package can therefore commit successfully and then conflict on an exact restart/retry, violating FR-040 and the acknowledgement-loss scenario. This HIGH implementation-owned regression requires correction and fresh convergence and quality review. Independent checks computed the full binary diff SHA-256, verified all pinned artifact hashes, inspected the complete story and correction diffs plus entity/configuration/migration/repository/tests, ran the focused atomic replay and communication-classification suites 9/9, and ran both working-tree and pinned-boundary git diff --check successfully; the compilation emitted documented existing warnings but no error. The published convergence evidence reports PostgreSQL tamper 7/7, atomic 28/28, migration 2/2, and no pending model changes, but those suites contain no multi-classification replay case. Source containment, scoped DI/disposal, cancellation rollback, safe XML prohibitions and bounds, ManagementAccess authorization, exact ordering outside this finding, Windows-host runtime pins, PostgreSQL-only Docker topology, and Story 12.3/CodeGraphContext exclusions showed no additional blocking defect. No security bypass, source-content leakage, Worker dispatch, Document generation, or authority conflict was found.
